Bun 1.3.12 `Bun.serve` supports `perMessageDeflate` (verified in `node_modules/bun-types/serve.d.ts:455-487`).

### Slice 1 — Transport diet: quantization + permessage-deflate

- `lib/net/codec.ts`: add `qPos(v)` (2 decimals) and `qAng(v)` (3 decimals) helpers.
- `server/room.ts`: apply in `collectPlayerPoses`/`collectMobPoses`/vehicle/projectile collectors, roster entries, and the mounted x/y/z in `buildSelfDelta`. Shadows/deadbands keep full precision.
- `lib/net/NetworkSession.ts`: quantize the 20 Hz pose send + `sendCmd` eye pose.
- `server/index.ts`: `websocket: { perMessageDeflate: { compress: "16KB", decompress: true }, ... }`. Browsers negotiate automatically; Bun's WS client (loadSim/netProbe) too. CPU on shared-cpu-2x for ≤24 sockets @20 Hz is negligible — verify with loadSim.
- Caveat to document: `Room.bytesOut` counts pre-compression bytes, so `/rooms` shows the quantization win only; verify deflate in DevTools (`Sec-WebSocket-Extensions`).
- Tests: quantizer round-trips; `server/room.test.ts` pose assertions updated to quantized values; handshake smoke still green with deflate on.
- Commit: `net: quantize replicated poses and enable permessage-deflate`

### Slice 2 — Jittered latency sim + F3 net stats (tooling before the features it verifies)

- `NetworkSession.setSimulatedLatency(ms, jitterMs?)` — per-message delay `max(0, ms + (rand*2-1)*jitter)`, **FIFO preserved** via a per-direction monotonic `lastScheduledDeliveryMs` (TCP never reorders; `applyBlocks`/seq assume order). Env: `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_JITTER_MS` beside the existing latency var (`NetworkSession.ts:118-119`). `Math.random` is fine (frame-local, never seed-determined).
- `netStats(): { rttMs, jitterMs, interpDelayMs, inKBps, outKBps, pendingPredictions }` on the session; byte counters in `delayedSend`/`processServerFrame` (2 s rolling window).
- `components/game/DebugOverlay.tsx`: optional `net` prop (pass `online` from `MinecraftGame.tsx:147`), poll at 500 ms, two lines (RTT/jitter/interp, in/out KB/s, pending predictions).
- Tests: jitter never reorders (extend the existing sim-latency test in `lib/net/NetworkSession.test.ts`); netStats counts bytes.
- Commit: `net: jittered latency simulation and F3 net stats`

### Slice 3 — Clock hardening + adaptive interpolation delay

- `lib/net/clock.ts`: keep the `ClockSync` surface. Offset = the offset of the **min-RTT sample** in a 16-pong ring (NTP-style best sample — least asymmetry), applied with slew: `OFFSET_WINDOW_SIZE=16`, `OFFSET_SLEW_MS_PER_SEC=40`, snap when error > `OFFSET_SNAP_MS=250` (first sample/reconnect snap). RTT stays EWMA for display + prediction timeouts.
- Ping cadence 2000 → `PING_INTERVAL_MS = 1000` (extract constant, `NetworkSession.ts:623`).
- `lib/net/interpolation.ts`: `createDelayController(nominalMs=50)` — `onTickArrival(nowMs, tickN)` (tick-number-aware so a coalesced TCP burst counts once; ignore non-increasing `n`), jitter = p90 of `|Δarrival − Δtick×50|` over a 64-sample ring, target = `clamp(50 + 2×p90, 125, 450)`, `effectiveDelayMs()` slews at 60 ms/s. Constants: `INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MIN_MS=125` (old fixed value becomes the floor), `INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MAX_MS=450`, `INTERPOLATION_JITTER_MULT=2`, `DELAY_SLEW_MS_PER_SEC=60`. `BUFFER_SIZE=32` (1.6 s) already covers 450 ms.
- Wire in `NetworkSession`: `onTickArrival` in the tick case; `renderTime = serverTime - delayCtl.effectiveDelayMs(nowMs)` in `afterFrame` (line 628); reset window on `worldSync` (reconnect).
- Tests: move the clock describe out of `lib/net/protocol.test.ts` into new `lib/net/clock.test.ts` (asymmetric-jitter offset accuracy, slew bound, snap); `interpolation.test.ts` controller convergence both directions; NetworkSession jittered-arrival no-freeze test.
- Commit: `net: adaptive interpolation delay and min-RTT clock sync`

### Slice 4 — Server event attribution (prerequisite for echo dedup)

- `lib/game/engine/state.ts`: `AttributedGameEvent = GameEvent & { playerId?: PlayerId }`.
- `GameEngine.emit`: when `authority === "server"`, stamp `playerId` from existing `?? actorId ?? this.actingPlayer` (already scoped around `stepPlayer`/`dispatch`, `GameEngine.ts:577-582, 698-704`). Explicit playerIds (advancements, join/leave) win; shared-system events (mob AI, TNT) stay unattributed; single-player untouched. `Room.tick` needs no change.
- Tests: `room.test.ts` — `blockPlaced`/`attackSwung` in `ev` carry the actor's id; local engine doesn't stamp.
- Commit: `server: attribute tick events to the acting player`

### Slice 5 — Prediction ledger + optimistic block placement

- `lib/game/engine/blockChanges.ts`: journal becomes `Map<idx, {block, prev}>` (prev captured on first write per drain window); `drainEdits()` output unchanged for the server; add `drainEditsDetailed(): Array<{idx, block, prev}>`.
- New `lib/net/prediction.ts` (pure, DOM-free): `createPredictionLedger()` with `add(kind, edits, refund, nowMs, rttMs)`, `onJournal(idx, block) → {refunds}` (any journal write to an idx resolves every prediction touching it: match ⇒ confirm edit, all-confirmed ⇒ retire; mismatch ⇒ drop prediction + collect refund; never mutates the world), `expire(nowMs) → Prediction[]`, `shouldSuppress(idx, nowMs)` (separate map, window = deadline + `ECHO_SUPPRESS_EXTRA_MS=3000` — must outlive confirm since the echo rides the same tick), `clear()`, `size()`. Timeout: `clamp(2×rtt+200, 1000, 5000)`.
- `GameEngine.predictPlaceBlock()` (replica-only): conservative gates — held slot is a placeable block (excludes spear/boat/hoe/seeds/food/rod/totem branches of the overloaded right-click, `GameEngine.ts:879-906`), no mob/vehicle near the aim ray, target not in `INTERACTIVE_BLOCKS` (`interact.ts:33` — doors/beds/stations/chests), alive + `canEditBlocks`. Then flush the never-drained replica journal, run the real `placeSelectedBlock` (validates, consumes stack, emits `blockPlaced` → instant local sound/particles), drain detailed → edits + refund. Gate fails ⇒ return null = status quo (server handles it). **Always `sendCmd` regardless.**
- `NetworkSession`: `routeDispatch` predicts before sending; `applyBlocks` runs `ledger.onJournal` per pair, applies refunds via `adjustSlotCount`, skips redundant same-value writes, then discard-drains (server writes aren't predictions); timeout sweep in `afterFrame` reverts unconfirmed edits newest-first through `blockChanges.set` (relights free) + refunds; `ledger.clear()` on `worldSync`. Suppress own-attributed `blockPlaced`/`blockBroken` in the tick `ev` loop when `shouldSuppress(idx)`.
- Edge cases handled: rejected place (no journal, no delta) → timeout revert + refund; lost race → immediate override + refund, next inventory delta corrects; refund into a full inventory → drop silently (next full delta reconciles); predictions gated on socket OPEN; door = 2 edits, retires only when both confirm.
- Tests: `lib/net/prediction.test.ts` (confirm/multi-edit/override/expire/suppress/clear); `drainEditsDetailed` prev-capture; NetworkSession end-to-end fake-socket cases (instant place, confirm-no-revert + echo suppressed, mismatch override, timeout revert restores block + item, worldSync clears). Update the existing "routes gameplay commands…" test (placeBlock now also mutates the replica).
- Commit: `net: optimistic block placement with a prediction ledger`

### Slice 6 — Predictive block breaking + instant swing

- `lib/game/engine/systems/mining.ts`: `{cosmetic: true}` becomes `{authority: "full" | "cosmetic" | "predict"}`. `"predict"` (replica step): at full progress commit a **reduced** break — block write via `blockChanges.set` + `blockBroken` emit (instant crack-out sound/particles), **no** drops/XP/durability/chest-spill. **Chests excluded** (fall back to cosmetic cap — container entanglement isn't worth it). Creative replica predicts instant break too.
- `NetworkSession.afterFrame`: drain `drainEditsDetailed()` right after the engine step — any entries there are mining commits (place/applyBlocks/revert paths drain inline) → `ledger.add("break", …)`. Confirm/override/timeout ride Slice 5 unchanged. Server mines from streamed `mineHeld` a tick or two skewed — journal confirms whenever it lands; if server aim resolved a different voxel, ours reverts on timeout while the real one applies unsuppressed. Drops stay server-owned (hotbar count lags ~RTT; documented).
- Cosmetic `attack`: `routeDispatch` pushes a synthetic `attackSwung` into `pendingEvents` before `sendCmd`; suppress own-attributed `attackSwung` echoes. No hit/damage prediction.
- Tests: mining `"predict"` mode (commit without inventory/XP; chest caps like cosmetic; kelp multi-cell); NetworkSession predicted-break confirm/revert; swing echo suppressed.
- Commit: `net: predictive block breaking and instant swing feedback`

### Slice 7 — Verification pass + docs sweep

- Full gate: `bun run lint` + `typecheck` + `format:check` + `bun test` + `bun run build`; `bun run test:e2e` (this touches renderer-adjacent + input paths). **Watch: `bun test` exit 99 = passed-but-leaked; don't pipe to tail.** Check port 3000 isn't held by another dev server before e2e (`lsof`).
- E2E: extend the existing two-context multiplayer test — `setSimulatedLatency(400, 100)` on the friend, place a block, assert the friend's own engine world has it within a few frames (engine-state assertion, not pixels) and the host converges within ~3 s; reset to 0. Drop to manual if flaky in CI (note in PR).
- Manual pass (two browsers, one at `setSimulatedLatency(450, 100)` ≈ 900 ms): instant place/break on the lagged client, no doubled sounds, racing the same voxel reverts the loser within ~2 s with item back, remote avatars smooth with F3 interp climbing to ~300–450 ms, chests/doors/feeding still work (delayed, correct), reconnect clears predictions.
- loadSim 8 clients before/after: `slowestTickMs` (deflate CPU ≈ noise) and `kbOutPerSec` (expect ~40–60% pre-compression cut); numbers in the PR description.
- Docs (per-slice, confirmed here): `docs/protocol.md` (quantization/deflate note, event attribution, prediction note in trust model), `docs/architecture.md` (multiplayer client: prediction ledger, predictive mining, adaptive delay, min-RTT clock), `docs/tuning.md` (all new constants + bytesOut caveat + sim jitter arg), `docs/testing.md` (new test files), `.env.example` (`NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_JITTER_MS`), `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Commit: `net: latency e2e coverage and tuning docs`

### Ops (after the branch merges): region move to US West

- `server/fly.toml`: `primary_region = 'ord'` → `'sjc'` (alternate `sea`/`lax` if measured worse from Asia). Rides the already-pending redeploy for the 512 MB VM change.
- **Critical invariant: exactly one machine.** After the region deploy, `fly machines list` must show a single machine in the new region — destroy any `ord` leftover (`fly scale count 1`). A second machine silently split-brains rooms (2026-07-05 incident).
- Verify: Asia + NA player each check the ping badge; expect ~200–400 ms Asia (route-dependent), 60–100 ms NA. Doc: `docs/deploy.md` region note if it names ord.

## Out of scope (explicit future work)

- **Server-side lag compensation** (rewind hit-testing): combat at 300+ ms still feels delayed; cosmetic swing is the only concession here.
- **Binary tick packing**: after quantization + deflate a tick frame is a few hundred bytes at 20 Hz — RTT-dominated, not payload-dominated; the envelope keeps the door open (protocol.md already says so).
- **Multi-region room affinity**: the real fix for permanently mixed-continent groups; an infra project.

## Risks

- Slices 5–6 touch the engine, but every change is replica- or drain-additive; the server's `drainEdits()` contract and single-player behavior stay byte-identical.
- Attribution (Slice 4) must be live on the server before predicting clients — one branch/one release satisfies this.
- `engine.consumeEvents()` discards in `upsertRemotePlayer`/`applyRoster` could swallow a predicted sound if a join echo interleaves (pre-existing pattern) — if it bites in testing, narrow those discards to join/leave events only.

# Wire protocol (v2)

The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.

## Transport & framing

WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
contract, not the encoding.

## Handshake

1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).

A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.

## Steady state

**Client → server**

- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
  distance stats, and fall damage.
- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.
- `kick { targetId }` — **owner-only**: eject a player. The server re-checks
  the sender's ticket `role` (same gate as the owner-wide `setDifficulty`/
  `setGameMode`), so a forged kick from a member is dropped; self-kick is a
  no-op. The `welcome` carries the recipient's own `role`, so the client shows
  the control only to the owner.

**Server → client**

- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, vp?, prj?, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since
  last tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob
  poses (~10 Hz), **vehicle poses** (`vp`, deadbanded — a parked boat costs
  nothing; vehicles never despawn so no absence-pruning), **arrow poses**
  (`prj`, the full live set every tick — arrows are few and fast, so they snap
  and prune by absence; one trailing empty `prj` clears the last one), the day
  clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-authoritative delta of
  YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…), sent only on change.
- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.

**Vehicles & mounted riders (v2).** A vehicle's pose (`VehiclePose`: id, kind,
x/y/z, yaw, riderId) replicates on `vp` and in the join `worldSync` (keyed by
server id, so per-tick deltas line up). Arrows (`ProjectilePose`: id, x/y/z,
vx/vy/vz — velocity so the client orients the mesh) replicate on `prj`. A
**mounted** rider is the one hybrid-model exception: the server owns their
position (`tickVehicles` drives it from their input intents), so the pose
stream is rejected without a `forcePose` correction, and the `SelfDelta`
carries `mountedVehicleId` (on mount/dismount) plus the authoritative `x/y/z`
(while mounted). The replica adopts that mount state and snaps to the position,
skipping its own motion integration until it dismounts.

Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp`/`vp`/`prj` are shed
(events and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

## Reconnect

The replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client
walks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a
**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole
new `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a
new socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the
same room in place. The server closes the player's _previous_ socket with
`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket
path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh
world-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is
exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.

## Close codes

| Code | Meaning                                           | Client retries? |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          | no (fatal)      |
| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         | no (fatal)      |
| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      | no (fatal)      |
| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) | no (fatal)      |
| 4004 | idle timeout                                      | yes (ladder)    |
| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) | yes (ladder)    |
| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              | no (fatal)      |
| 1006 | abnormal close (network drop)                     | yes (ladder)    |

## Trust model

The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
rewind validation would need.

`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS`, `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, `SAVE_KEY` (legacy), `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`,
`RENDER_RADIUS`, `RENDER_GRID`, `THIRD_PERSON_DISTANCE`, `THIRD_PERSON_MARGIN`.

`RENDER_RADIUS` is the biggest **performance** lever: the renderer meshes one region
of this radius around the player, so larger values draw more terrain at higher cost;
`RENDER_GRID` is how far the player moves before that mesh rebuilds (smaller = more
frequent rebuilds, fresher view). `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS` is how long an overlap is

## Multiplayer networking

Server-side constants live in `server/room.ts` and `lib/net/protocol.ts` (not
`config.ts` — they shape the wire and the room budget, not gameplay balance).
None affect single-player, and none are save-sensitive.

- **`ROOM_CAPACITY`** (`8`, protocol.ts) — max players per world. The v1 co-op
  scale the whole design assumes; raising it grows the per-tick pose/self fan-out
  quadratically, so re-measure with `loadSim` before nudging it.
- **`MAX_ROOMS`** (env, default `6`) — worlds one process hosts (memory: ~74 MB
  each). Joins beyond it are refused at the door, not thrashed. Tune from
  `/rooms` p95 tick + peak memory.
- **Tick rate** — `TICK_SECONDS` (`0.05` = 20 Hz, `tickDriver.ts`) is the room
  sim + pose-stream cadence. The whole latency budget hangs off it; not a
  casual dial.
- **Replication cadence** — `KEYFRAME_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`100` = 5 s, full mob
  keyframe / drift correction), mob delta frames at **10 Hz** (half tick rate)
  with `MOB_DEADBAND_SQ` (`0.05²` — smaller = more mob updates, more bandwidth),
  `DAY_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`20` = 1 s day-clock sync), `POSE_CHECKPOINT_TICKS`
  (`20` = 1 s replay-log pose anchors). `INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MS` (`125`,
  `lib/net/interpolation.ts`) is how far in the past remote entities render —
  larger absorbs more jitter at the cost of visible lag.
- **Backpressure** — `BACKPRESSURE_SOFT_BYTES` (256 KB → shed `pp`/`mp`),
  `BACKPRESSURE_KICK_BYTES` (1 MB) + `BACKPRESSURE_KICK_STRIKES` (~5 s sustained
  → `4008` kick).

The `welcome` frame now carries each player's own role.
29	- **Online co-op parity — per-player progression, kill credit & pets**: each player in a shared world now earns their **own** advancements and statistics (the engine attributes an emitted gameplay event to whoever's per-player step or command is running, so a co-op room scores everyone independently instead of accruing nothing) and gets credit for their **own** kills — melee, arrow, spear, or a companion pet's bite — tracked on the mob so even a delayed death (a daylight burn, an explosion softened by your earlier hit) credits the right player, paying them the loot and XP. Your advancement set and stats sync privately over the `SelfDelta`, advancement toasts are tagged so you only see your own, and **pets follow their owner** rather than trailing the nearest player. Single-player is unchanged.
30	- **Online co-op parity — vehicles & arrows (protocol v1→v2)**: rafts and ships are now boardable in a shared world, and in-flight arrows are replicated (not just their hits). Vehicles and arrows travel on their own per-tick channels (`vp`/`prj`, mirroring the mob-pose skeleton) and the join world-sync, so the existing renderer draws them unchanged. A **mounted** rider is the one hybrid-model exception: the server owns their position (driven from their input intents) and streams it on the private `SelfDelta` (`mountedVehicleId` + authoritative position), so the client replica stops predicting its own motion while mounted rather than rubber-banding against the boat — and the server no longer answers a mounted player's (expected-rejected) pose with a `forcePose` snap-back. perf(net): quantize replicated poses and enable permessage-deflate

Raw doubles serialize at up to 17 chars per coordinate, and the 20 Hz
tick frames went out as uncompressed JSON — wasteful on any link and
actively harmful on congested intercontinental routes, where every
queued byte adds delay ahead of the frames behind it.

serialization sites only (server shadows and deadbands keep full
precision), and offer permessage-deflate from Bun.serve — browsers
negotiate it automatically, and the repetitive JSON keys compress 3-5x.
Same envelope, no protocol bump; old and new clients interoperate.

1	# Tuning & Balance
2	
3	Every gameplay tunable lives in one place: [`lib/game/config.ts`](../lib/game/config.ts).
4	Each constant there carries a one-line comment; this guide is the companion that
5	groups them by **what they affect**, names the **system that reads each**, and
6	flags the **balance trade-offs** and the few that are **save-sensitive**.
7	
8	To rebalance, edit `config.ts` — not the systems. Item-level numbers (a pickaxe's
9	power, a sword's damage, a food's hunger) are **not** here; they live with the
10	content in [`items.ts`](../lib/game/items.ts) (see the [reference](reference.md)).
11	Worldgen constants live in the frozen `GEN` object in
12	[`generation.ts`](../lib/world/generation.ts) and are pinned by hash tests — see
13	[testing.md](testing.md).
14	
15	## Player feel — physics & movement
16	
17	`GRAVITY`, `JUMP_VELOCITY`, `WALK_SPEED`, `SPRINT_SPEED`, `CROUCH_SPEED`,
18	`PLAYER_HEIGHT`, `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`, `EYE_HEIGHT`, `WORLD_BORDER_PADDING`.
19	
20	Read by `systems/playerMotion.ts`. These set the moment-to-moment feel.
21	`JUMP_VELOCITY` vs `GRAVITY` together fix jump height (currently a ~1-block hop);
22	raise gravity for a snappier, heavier fall. `SPRINT_SPEED` is deliberately far
23	above `WALK_SPEED` so sprinting feels like a meaningful choice (and it's what burns
24	hunger fastest). `PLAYER_HALF_WIDTH`/`PLAYER_HEIGHT` are also the collision box, so
25	changing them affects which gaps the player fits through.
26	
27	## Water vehicles
28	
29	`VEHICLE_BOARD_REACH`, `VEHICLE_TURN_RATE`, `VEHICLE_DISMOUNT_RADIUS`,
30	`RAFT_SPEED`, `RAFT_HALF_WIDTH`, `RAFT_HALF_LENGTH`, `SHIP_SPEED`,
31	`SHIP_HALF_WIDTH`, `SHIP_HALF_LENGTH`, `MAX_VEHICLES`.
32	
33	Read by `systems/vehicles.ts`. Rafts are intentionally compact and slow; ships
34	are larger and faster. The half-width/half-length values are both gameplay
35	footprints and water-support checks, so raising them makes a vehicle feel larger
36	but also requires more open water to place and move. `VEHICLE_TURN_RATE` controls
37	steering responsiveness while mounted, and `VEHICLE_DISMOUNT_RADIUS` is the search
38	radius for a safe crouch dismount beside the vehicle. `MAX_VEHICLES` (64) caps how
39	many placed rafts/ships a world can hold — placement is refused (with a denial
40	cue) at the cap, which bounds save size since creative placement never consumes
41	the item.
42	
43	## Game modes — flight
44	
45	`FLY_SPEED`, `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS`.
46	
47	Used by the flight path in `systems/playerMotion.ts` and the double-tap detector
48	in `input/inputController.ts`. `FLY_SPEED` is the vertical climb/descend speed
49	while flying (Creative and Spectator); horizontal speed still comes from
50	`WALK_SPEED`/`SPRINT_SPEED`. `FLY_DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW_SECONDS` is how close two
51	`Space` presses must be to toggle flight — raise it if a double-tap feels hard to
52	trigger, lower it if flight toggles by accident while bunny-hopping. (The modes
53	themselves and their gates live in `lib/game/gameModes.ts`, not `config.ts`.)
54	
55	## Survival pressure — the main difficulty dial
56	
57	`MAX_HEARTS`, `MAX_HUNGER`, `RESPAWN_SECONDS`, `HEALTH_REGEN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
58	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER`, `SPRINT_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`,
59	`WALK_BLOCKS_PER_HUNGER`, `JUMPS_PER_HUNGER`, `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
60	`STARVATION_HP`, `WATER_DAMAGE_DELAY_SECONDS`, `WATER_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`,
61	`WATER_DAMAGE_HP`.
62	
63	Read by `systems/playerStats.ts` (drain + regen) and `systems/playerLife.ts`
64	(respawn). This group is where "how hard is it to stay alive" is set. The
65	`*_PER_HUNGER` budgets control how fast activity drains food — lower numbers = more
66	eating. The two gates are the key feedback loop: you must stay above
67	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER` (12) to heal and above `SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` (6) to sprint, so
68	hunger pressure indirectly throttles both combat recovery and escape speed. Keep
69	`REGEN_MIN_HUNGER > SPRINT_MIN_HUNGER` so there's a "can run but can't heal" band.
70	Water exposure is continuous body-midpoint immersion: leaving water resets both
71	timers. After `WATER_DAMAGE_DELAY_SECONDS` (60), environmental damage bypasses
72	armor every `WATER_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (1) for `WATER_DAMAGE_HP` (3 HP = 1.5
73	hearts). These counters are transient and reset on reload/respawn.
74	**Starvation** is the consequence of a fully-empty hunger bar: once `hunger` hits
75	0, `STARVATION_HP` (1 HP) is lost every `STARVATION_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (4) down to a
76	**difficulty-scaled floor** (see below) — these two constants are the cadence; the
77	floor is the per-level dial.
78	
79	## Difficulty — Peaceful / Easy / Normal / Hard
80	
81	The per-level multipliers live in `lib/game/difficulties.ts` (accessor functions,
82	not `config.ts` constants — the _base_ values they bend stay in `config.ts`). It is
83	an axis orthogonal to game mode, picked at world creation and switchable in the
84	pause menu; the spawn directors and mob AI read `state.difficulty` every tick.
85	
86	| Dial (accessor)                       | Peaceful | Easy | Normal | Hard |
87	| ------------------------------------- | -------- | ---- | ------ | ---- |
88	| `hostilesSpawn`                       | no       | yes  | yes    | yes  |
89	| `mobDamageMultiplier` (×hit)          | —        | 0.5  | 1      | 1.5  |
90	| `hostileSpawnIntervalScale`           | —        | 1.5  | 1      | 0.6  |
91	| `hostileCapScale` (×`HOSTILE_CAP` 16) | 0        | 8    | 16     | 24   |
92	| `regenIntervalScale` (×regen)         | 0.5      | 1    | 1      | 1    |
93	| `starvationFloorHp` (HP floor)        | never    | 10   | 1      | 0    |
94	
95	Read by `systems/spawnDirector.ts` (the spawn gate + cadence/cap scales),
96	`systems/mobAI.ts` (the per-hit damage scale, applied at the strike — templates are
97	never mutated), and `systems/playerStats.ts` (faster Peaceful regen + the
98	starvation floor). **Peaceful** also despawns existing hostiles the moment you
99	switch to it (`GameEngine.switchDifficulty`). Note these dials are independent of
100	game mode: Peaceful stops hostile _spawns_ regardless of mode, while damage/threat
101	still gate on the mode (Creative is invulnerable at any difficulty). The **Hardcore**
102	flag (a per-world boolean, not a tunable) forces this dial to Hard and locks it — see
103	`docs/architecture.md` for the permadeath/game-over flow.
104	
105	## Cave hazards — lava & drowning
106	
107	`LAVA_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `LAVA_DAMAGE_HP`, `LAVA_BURN_SECONDS`,
108	`MAX_OXYGEN`, `OXYGEN_HOLD_SECONDS`, `OXYGEN_REFILL_SECONDS`,
109	`OXYGEN_DROWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, `OXYGEN_DROWN_HP`.
110	
111	Read by `systems/playerStats.ts` (`tickLavaExposure`, `tickOxygen`), both on the
112	armor-bypassing damage path. **Lava** burns the instant you touch it (no grace
113	period, unlike water) for `LAVA_DAMAGE_HP` (6 = 3 hearts) every
114	`LAVA_DAMAGE_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (0.5) and keeps burning `LAVA_BURN_SECONDS` (3)
115	after you escape — the deep-cave death trap. Lava is solid, so contact is checked
116	underfoot/at the body, not by immersion. **Drowning** keys on the head: the
117	bubble meter drains over `OXYGEN_HOLD_SECONDS` (15) while the eye cell is
118	underwater, then deals `OXYGEN_DROWN_HP` (2) every `OXYGEN_DROWN_INTERVAL_SECONDS`
119	(1); surfacing refills it over `OXYGEN_REFILL_SECONDS` (1.5). This is separate
120	from the body-keyed 60 s water-exposure timer above — wading chest-deep never
121	drowns you. All these counters are transient (reset on reload/respawn).
122	
123	Lighting itself has no `config.ts` tunables: the per-voxel light propagation is
124	in [`lib/world/lighting.ts`](../lib/world/lighting.ts) (block opacity/emission and
125	the 0–15 levels), and the cave-darkness floor + torch tint are shader constants in
126	[`GameRenderer.ts`](../lib/game/render/GameRenderer.ts) (`SKY_LIGHT_FLOOR`,
127	`TORCH_TINT`).
128	
129	## Status effects & potions
130	
131	`EFFECT_SPEED_DURATION`/`EFFECT_SPEED_MULTIPLIER`,
132	`EFFECT_STRENGTH_DURATION`/`EFFECT_STRENGTH_BONUS`,
133	`EFFECT_REGEN_DURATION`/`EFFECT_REGEN_INTERVAL`/`EFFECT_REGEN_HP`,
134	`EFFECT_FIRE_RESIST_DURATION`, `EFFECT_WATER_BREATHING_DURATION`,

lines: - **Zero-config local dev**: `bun run dev` with no `DATABASE_URL` now falls back to an ephemeral in-memory PGlite database (with a one-time console notice) instead of 500-ing on the first online request — the full accounts/cloud-saves stack works out of the box in dev, resetting on restart. Production still requires a real `DATABASE_URL`.

+- **Net debug tooling — jittered latency simulation + F3 connection stats**: `window.__monecraft.net.setSimulatedLatency(ms, jitterMs)` now takes an optional per-message jitter (delivery stays FIFO, like real TCP), seedable via `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_JITTER_MS`, and the F3 overlay gains two lines while online — RTT/jitter/interpolation delay and in/out KB/s — so high-latency play can be reproduced and observed locally instead of across an ocean.
